text.usage_text: Pun Dog is a three-panel image macro series featuring photographs of an Alaskan Klee Kai dog with animal-themed puns and anticlimactic punchlines, in a similar vein to the advice animal characters Bad Joke Eel and Lame Pun Coon.

text.visual_description: The image features the head of an owl prominently in the center, holding a cigarette in its beak. The background consists of alternating triangles of dark blue and ochre colors radiating from the center, commonly associated with impactful, attention-grabbing presentation.
text.usage_text: Art Student Owl is an advice animal image macro series featuring an owl with a cigarette in its mouth. The overlaid text typically makes fun of art student stereotypes or conveys frustrations commonly shared by artists and students in art school.

text.visual_description: The scene predominantly features the head of a cat against a vibrant background of alternating orange and yellow radial stripes. The cat's face is prominent, with wide-open eyes and an open mouth, suggesting it is either meowing or expressing surprise.
text.usage_text: Bad Advice Cat is an advice animal image macro series, with a cat recommending terrible or inane solutions to life's problems, similar to Advice Dog.

text.visual_description: The scene captures a young man running in a marathon, surrounded by other runners. His main action is running, with a clear focus on the expression of joy or enthusiasm on his face.
text.usage_text: Ridiculously Photogenic Guy (RPG) is a Photoshop meme and advice animal featuring a photo of a smiling man called Zeddie Little running in the 2012 Cooper River Bridge Run. The photo gained notoriety online after being posted to the social news website Reddit, where users found the man to be exceptionally handsome.

text.visual_description: The scene features a determined-looking individual wearing a sheriff's uniform and hat, pointing a revolver directly forward. This character is prominent in the foreground against a blurred backdrop of muted yellow hues, giving the image a tense and dramatic atmosphere.
text.usage_text: Hasta La Vista, Zombie refers to a series of memes based on a three-panel image macro depicting Rick Grimes (played by actor Andrew Lincoln) from The Walking Dead aiming his gun at a zombie and saying, "Hasta la vista zombie," in the first panel, the zombie then telling Grimes he likes something in the second, followed by Grimes and the zombie posing for a photo together after the zombie successfully convinces Grimes not to shoot her. The original meme was posted to Facebook as early as 2017 and became the subject of photoshops over the following years, often altering the caption associated with the zombie.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a young female character prominently positioned against a background of diagonal pink rays. She is wearing large, thick-framed glasses and holding her hand up with the text "NERD" written on her palm.
text.usage_text: Idiot Nerd Girl is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a teenage girl wearing thick-rimmed glasses with the word "NERD" written on the palm of her left hand. The upper caption often contains references to "geek culture," while the bottom caption demonstrates a lack of knowledge or expertise in the subject. The series bears many similarities to the Technologically Impaired Duck and Musically Oblivious 8th Grader advice animals.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a comic-style character with exaggerated facial features, including a wide, toothy grin and thick beard, wearing a golden helmet. The character is giving a thumbs-up gesture, which complements his enthusiastic expression.
text.usage_text: "Cool Story, Bro" is a catchphrase often seen in image macros as a sarcastic response on message boards or in comments to posts that are deemed boring, pointless, or too long to read (TL;DR).

name: Keep Calm And Carry On Aqua

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image consists of a minimalist design featuring a simple crown emblem centered near the top of a solid turquoise background. There are no characters or complex actions depicted; instead, the image is iconic and static with no additional decorations or figures.
text.usage_text: Keep Calm and Carry On is a catchphrase that originally appeared on a World War II-era British public safety poster. After one of the original posters was recovered and placed in a British bookshop in 2000, the inspirational message was shared online, sparking a series of image macros centered around the phrasal template "Keep Calm and X."

text.visual_description: The image features a simple, stick-figure character with an exaggerated, smug expression, appearing somewhat like a comic sketch. Its arms are slightly raised, conveying a stance of self-satisfaction or defiance.
text.usage_text: Close Enough is a rage comic character that is used to convey mild satisfaction towards the outcome of a situation, despite not having achieved a result that would be considered ideal. The character's facial expression is derived from another rage comic series called Fuck Yeah.

text.visual_description: The image shows a young man wearing a blue shirt with an upturned collar. He has short light brown hair and appears to be looking upwards and to the right.
text.usage_text: Misunderstood D-Bag (sometimes known as Misunderstood Mitch) is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photograph of a man wearing a blue polo shirt with an erect collar and "soul patch" facial hair. The caption at the top describes stereotypical frat-boy behaviors reminiscent of Scumbag Steve, followed by the bottom caption offering a convenient excuse that somehow justifies the aforementioned deed, similar to the twist in Successful Black Man captions.

text.visual_description: The image features the head of a dog with dark brown and black fur, prominently displayed against a radial background that fades from dark to light. The dog's eyes are wide open, conveying a sense of surprise or alertness, and its ears are perked up, suggesting attentiveness.
text.usage_text: Depression Dog is an advice animal-style image macro featuring a cutout photo of a taxidermic dog on a color wheel background with shades of gray. The captions typically present bleak situations with a downtrodden outlook, similar to Forever Alone image macros.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image centers on a single character depicted in a monochrome, sketch-like style with exaggerated, bold lines. The character is shown with an upward-angled face, wide eyes, and an open mouth, suggesting a reaction to something shocking or horrifying.
text.usage_text: The "Oh Crap" or "OMG Face" refers to an exploitable image used in rage comics to express an array of feelings, including astonishment, revelation, or sheer rage. It is often paired with red or white text, summing up the character's thoughts. It is also used to represent a Gropaga [7], or follower of Inglip.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image focuses on a young boy with a gentle smile standing in an outdoor setting. The main character is looking directly at the camera, giving the viewer a sense of engagement.
text.usage_text: Annoying Childhood Friend is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a young boy in a white polo shirt smiling at the camera. Like a younger version of Scumbag Steve, the captions typically portray the character as an inconsiderate host, a demanding guest, or an obnoxious playmate.

text.visual_description: The scene core involves a singular male character depicted in a highly exaggerated manner, reminiscent of a black-and-white comic or line drawing. The character is captured in the midst of laughing heartily, with his head tilted back and mouth wide open.
text.usage_text: Aww Yea Guy is a character found in webcomics, based on a drawing of a complacent-looking man leaning backwards and shouting "AAAWWW YYYEEAA." This image is typically used to express a feeling of accomplishment or success in various situations, most notably through Ragetoon comics or other four-pane images. Also see: Fuck Yeah Guy.

text.visual_description: The image features a black-and-white illustration of a man's face. The man appears to have short, dark hair and a neatly trimmed goatee.
text.usage_text: Are You Serious Face, also known as "Seriously?", is a black and white drawing of a perplexed-looking man or woman that is often used in rage comics. It is generally used as a reaction to overwhelming ignorance or stupidity.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image consists of the iconic Skype logo displayed prominently in the center against a blue background. The main elements are the stylized word "Skype" in white, bold letters, and the abstract figure resembling a person, also in shades of blue and white, which is often associated with the brand.
text.usage_text: Skype is an instant messaging, video chat, and voice call application for Microsoft Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, Blackberry, and iOS platforms.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this meme template features a single cartoonish character known as "Forever Alone," represented by a simple hand-drawn face with exaggerated, tearful eyes and a wide, sad smile. The character appears to be stationary, with no actions taking place.
text.usage_text: Forever Alone is an exploitable rage comic character that is used to express loneliness and disappointment with life. The face has also been used as an advice animal and inspired the creation of the snowclone template "Forever an X."

text.visual_description: The core scene of the image features a simply drawn cartoon face with large, wide eyes and a small, straight mouth, which appears somewhat perplexed or confused. The character is not engaged in any particular action other than looking outward, directly at the viewer.
text.usage_text: What Did I Just Read is an image/Rage Comic that takes a piece of text that is awkward and then puts a picture of a derp guy smiling and then puts the text "What did I just read?"

text.visual_description: The image presents a simplistic, black-and-white drawing of a face with exaggerated, cartoonish features. The character has a round head and intense facial expression with large, upturned eyebrows, narrowed eyes, and a frown, which suggests a strong, determined attitude.
text.usage_text: Determined Guy is a Rage Comics face used to convey that the person is determined, serious, and/or threatening. It was originally supposed to convey mild annoyance.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a stick figure character in a triumphant pose. The figure stands with its head slightly tilted back and fists clenched slightly beside its body, as if ready for action or celebrating an achievement.
text.usage_text: Fuck Yeah is a series of four-pane cartoon strips featuring a stick figure looking complacent and confident. Originally posted via /b/ board in February 2010, these cartoons illustrate triumphant moments. This phenomenon can also be seen as the antithesis to Rage Guy comics, another four-pane series originating from 4chan circa late 2008.

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a dirigible, which appears to be inflating or exploding, with flames dramatically erupting from the top. The blimp prominently displays the text "ROMNEY - BELIEVE IN AMERICA." The image seems to be a specific moment of disaster, capturing the explosion's intensity.
text.usage_text: The LZ 129 Hindenburg was a German passenger airship which exploded over New Jersey on May 6th, 1937. The disaster was famously observed by, among others, radio journalist Herbert Morrison, who very melodramatically described it in a narration famously played together with a separate filming of the event, forming what has since become the definitive audio-visual account. Morrison's speech contains the now-famous phrase "Oh, the humanity," which has since become a commonly repeated quote used to express shock and awe at disastrous events.

text.visual_description: The scene core of the image features a stylized pony character with a white body and shiny purple mane and tail, standing in a poised and confident posture. There is a prominent feature of a horn on its forehead, indicating it is a unicorn.
text.usage_text: Rarity is a major character in the Hasbro Canadian-American animated television series My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic. She is depicted as a light grey unicorn with a purple mane and a cutie mark consisting of three rhombus-shaped jewels. A notable aspect of her personality is her obsession with clothing and aesthetics in general.

text.visual_description: The image features a large, menacing face with exaggerated and grotesque features. The main character is an ominous figure with sharp, exaggerated teeth, a pronounced mustache, and intense, bulging eyes.
text.usage_text: "I Lied" is a nefarious-looking blue and black drawing of a face that is often used as the punchline of rage comics. It is meant to indicate that the subject in the comic has been dishonest in some way, often in a very insignificant "white lie."

text.visual_description: The scene core of this image features a cat dressed in human-like attire, wearing a purple hood and glasses. The cat’s face is the primary focus, with its eyes wide open, conveying a sense of awareness.
text.usage_text: Hipster Kitty (a.k.a. Hipster Cat) is an advice animal image macro series featuring a fashion-conscious kitten wearing a lavender hoodie and a pair of thick-framed glasses. The image macros are typically paired with tongue-in-cheek sayings to poke fun at the self-righteous lifestyles of vintage-loving, cheap beer-sipping, Bukowski-quoting urban demographics. To a certain extent, Hipster Kitty can be seen as a self-parody phenomenon.

text.visual_description: Scene Core: The image features a duck as the main character standing prominently against a vibrant, multicolored background that is divided into segments. The duck is in a natural upright posture with no additional props or text visible, highlighting its smooth feathers and the simple contrast between its white body and the various hues of orange, yellow, and red in the background.
text.usage_text: Technologically Impaired Duck is an Advice Animal image macro series featuring a centered image of a white duck with overlaid text conveying technological ignorance or misunderstanding.

text.visual_description: The image features a central, close-up view of a cicada’s face placed at the center of a radial, starburst pattern composed of alternating shades of teal and blue triangles. There are no human characters, and there is no visible text in the image.
text.usage_text: Crazy Girlfriend Praying Mantis is an advice animal image macro series featuring a photo of a praying mantis set against a blue and teal color wheel background. The overlaid text typically describes what an overbearing, irrational, or obsessive girlfriend might say to her significant other.

text.visual_description: The image features a round, blue spherical character with a highly exaggerated facial expression. The character has wide, manic eyes with small pupils and a broad, toothy grin that suggests intensity.
text.usage_text: "I Lied" is a nefarious-looking blue and black drawing of a face that is often used as the punchline of rage comics and is meant to indicate that the subject in the comic has been dishonest in some way, often in a very insignificant "white lie."

text.visual_description: The image features a crow with a top hat and a cane, positioned on a segmented purple and violet background. Beside it, there is a bottle, likely meant to depict wine or champagne.
text.usage_text: Rich Raven, also known as Carnegie Crow, is an Advice Animal image macro series featuring a raven with seemingly immense wealth. The text first references a luxury or highly desired item or situation, which Rich Raven then scoffs at disdainfully. Another variation refers to an everyday item but then presents a ridiculously luxurious version.

text.visual_description: The scene core features a central image of a young man's face, prominently placed against a brightly colored, radial background comprising alternating orange and gray triangular segments. The face is the primary focus, and no other characters or entities are present within the image.
text.usage_text: Advice Peeta is an image macro series featuring photos of the actor Josh Hutcherson, who played the character Peeta in the 2012 science fiction film "The Hunger Games." The captions typically use puns related to baking bread, which is the character's main talent in the story.

text.visual_description: The scene core consists of a single character, a stylized and exaggerated human-like face with a smooth, pale surface. The character's facial features are prominent, with notably large eyes and a slight frown.
text.usage_text: Everyone knows the "Okay" face. This is an "expansion" to it.

text.visual_description: The image depicts a simple yet expressive face drawn in a stylized, cartoon-like manner. The central character appears to have a round, bald head with exaggeratedly sad facial features.
text.usage_text: Okay Guy is a sullen-looking rage comic character who is typically accompanied by the caption "okay." The face is often used in the final panel of comics meant to convey a feeling of hopeless resignation.

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a man reclined on a lounge chair in a playful, outdoor setting, likely a park. He is wearing sunglasses, an orange vest, and pink shorts, exuding an air of relaxation and leisure.
text.usage_text: Gangnam Style (강남 스타일) is a 2012 dance pop single written and performed by Korean pop singer Park Jae Sung, better known by his stage name PSY. Since its release in mid-July 2012, the highly entertaining music video has spawned hundreds of parodies and copycat dance videos on YouTube and surpassed Justin Bieber's single "Baby" as the most watched video on YouTube with over one billion views as of December 21st, 2012.

text.visual_description: The image features a solitary male character who is wearing a leather jacket and sunglasses. He is depicted in a confident, almost swaggering posture, with his head turned slightly to the side as if he's addressing someone off-camera.
text.usage_text: Disruptive Durden, or "Helpful Tyler Durden," is an advice animal image macro series featuring a fan art painting of Tyler Durden, a character from the 1996 novel and the 1999 film adaptation of Fight Club, with captions describing ethically questionable deeds that end up helping someone else. (See also: Good Guy Greg)

text.visual_description: The scene depicts a man at the forefront of a bus or coach, energetically yelling or singing into the camera. He wears sunglasses and a white, buttoned shirt, drawing attention among several seated people, some who are also wearing sunglasses.
text.usage_text: Gangnam Style (강남 스타일) is a 2012 dance pop single written and performed by Korean pop singer Park Jae-sung, better known by his stage name PSY. Since its release in mid-July 2012, the highly entertaining music video has spawned hundreds of parodies and copycat dance videos on YouTube and surpassed Justin Bieber's single "Baby" as the most watched video on YouTube with over one billion views as of December 21, 2012.

text.visual_description: The image features a single male character with medium-length, curly brown hair and a slight beard. He appears to be wearing a dark-colored polo shirt.
text.usage_text: First discovered in December of 2010, Family Technical Support Guy is most popular due to its relatable nature with most of the meme-watching community. Most depictions include typical scenarios that are fueled by family members' typical incompetence with technology or unfathomable technologically complicated or unnecessary demands.

text.visual_description: The image is a minimalist cartoon drawing featuring a simplistic human-like figure with yellow hair styled with a small black bow. There are no detailed facial features, only basic lines indicating a smile.
